This vignette is a maintainer map for <code>llmshieldr</code>. It explains
where behavior lives, how data moves through the package, and what needs to
change when a contributor adds a detector, policy control, provider adapter,
or public function.

## Repository Map

```text
llmshieldr/
├── R/                    package implementation and roxygen documentation
├── man/                  generated Rd files; do not edit by hand
├── tests/testthat/       unit and regression tests
├── vignettes/            long-form user and developer guides
├── inst/extdata/         packaged example and security-evaluation data
├── inst/scripts/         opt-in benchmark scripts
├── demo/                 interactive demonstrations
├── DESCRIPTION           dependencies, package metadata, R version
├── NAMESPACE             generated exports and S3 registration
├── NEWS.md               user-facing development and release notes
├── README.Rmd            README source
├── README.md             generated repository landing page
└── _pkgdown.yml          reference and article navigation
```

Edit files under <code>R/</code>, tests, vignettes, and README sources.
Generate <code>man/</code> and <code>NAMESPACE</code> with roxygen2 after
changing exported interfaces.

## Runtime Layers

The implementation is split by responsibility:

| Layer | Main files |
|---|---|
| Core objects and findings | <code>R/rules.R</code> |
| Built-in policies | <code>R/policy.R</code>, <code>R/policy_controls.R</code> |
| Prompt and output scanning | <code>R/scan_prompt.R</code>, <code>R/scan_output.R</code> |
| Retrieved context | <code>R/scan_context.R</code>, <code>R/context_policy.R</code> |
| Conversation and documents | <code>R/conversation.R</code>, <code>R/documents.R</code> |
| Tools | <code>R/tool_guardrails.R</code>, <code>R/tool_policy.R</code> |
| Streaming | <code>R/streaming.R</code> |
| URL and output boundaries | <code>R/url_policy.R</code>, <code>R/output_contract.R</code> |
| Grounding | <code>R/grounding.R</code> |
| Optional scanners | <code>R/scanner_options.R</code>, <code>R/providers.R</code>, <code>R/secrets.R</code> |
| External adapters | <code>R/adapters.R</code>, <code>R/http.R</code> |
| Provider orchestration | <code>R/secure_chat.R</code> |
| Compatibility wrappers | <code>R/shield_gemini.R</code>, <code>R/shield_ollama.R</code> |
| Resource and trust controls | <code>R/rate_guard.R</code>, <code>R/trust_boundary.R</code> |
| Audit and telemetry | <code>R/audit.R</code>, <code>R/telemetry.R</code>, <code>R/stats.R</code> |
| Evaluation and taxonomy | <code>R/evaluation.R</code>, <code>R/owasp.R</code> |
| User explanations | <code>R/explain.R</code> |

## Execution Model

The high-level guarded flow is:

```text
prompt
  │
  ├─ scan_prompt()
  │
  ├─ scan_context() and context_policy()
  │
  ├─ rate_guard() reservation
  │
  ├─ assistant callback or ellmer provider
  │
  ├─ scan_output()
  │
  ├─ output_contract()
  │
  ├─ grounding_policy()
  │
  ├─ rate-guard update or rollback
  │
  └─ shieldr_result + shieldr_audit + telemetry events
```

<code>secure_chat()</code> owns this orchestration. Individual
<code>scan_*()</code> functions remain independently useful when an
application owns the model call or needs checks at one boundary.

Tool calls form another path:

```text
model tool request
  ├─ scan_tool_call()
  ├─ tool allowlist, schema, authorization, spend, and loop checks
  ├─ dispatcher
  └─ scan_tool_output()
```

## Public Object Contracts

The package uses inspectable S3 objects.

### shieldr_rule

One rule contains an ID, one regex or function, an OWASP category, severity,
action, description, and applicable stages. Exactly one of
<code>pattern</code> and <code>fn</code> must be present.

### shieldr_policy

A policy contains a name, rule list, thresholds, optional rate guard, optional
trusted sources, orchestration controls, and version. Built-in policy names are
resolved by <code>policy()</code>; application-owned policies are created with
<code>build_policy()</code> or <code>shieldr_policy()</code>.

### shieldr_report

A scanner report contains the resolved action, cleaned text, findings, risk
score, policy name, check mode, timestamp, optional token count, and
surface-specific metadata.

### shieldr_audit and shieldr_result

An audit collects input, context, tool, and output reports plus timing, token,
network, policy-version, and decision metadata. A result combines released
output, the audit, an OWASP risk summary, and the final orchestration action.

Keep these shapes backward compatible. When a new field is needed, prefer an
optional field with a safe default and update audit scrubbing and persistence
at the same time.

## Finding Schema

Detectors converge on a common finding structure:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| <code>rule_id</code> | Stable machine-readable identifier |
| <code>owasp</code> | Lowercase category such as <code>llm02</code> |
| <code>severity</code> | low, medium, high, or critical |
| <code>action</code> | allow, redact, or block |
| <code>description</code> | Human-readable reason |
| <code>match</code> | Optional matched evidence |
| <code>start</code>, <code>end</code> | Optional one-based character span |
| <code>source</code> | Rule, scanner, recognizer, provider, or reviewer |
| <code>confidence</code> | Optional calibrated detector value |

Content fields must be removed by metadata-only audit construction. New
evidence-bearing fields require the same privacy review.

## Adding a Deterministic Rule

1. Choose a stable OWASP-prefixed ID.
2. Limit the rule to relevant stages.
3. Choose regex matching when exact spans are useful.
4. Choose a function when structured logic is clearer.
5. Add a risky positive case.
6. Add a close benign case that guards against overblocking.
7. Test redaction spans when the action is redact.
8. Add a release note when built-in behavior changes.

```{r}
new_rule <- shieldr_rule(
  id = "llm02.project.identifier",
  pattern = "\\bPROJECT-[0-9]{6}\\b",
  owasp = "llm02",
  severity = "medium",
  action = "redact",
  description = "Internal project identifier.",
  stages = c("prompt", "context", "output")
)
```

Rule changes require detection and overblocking evidence. A broad expression
that catches the reported example but blocks ordinary domain text is
incomplete.

## Adding an Entity Recognizer

An entity recognizer receives one text string and returns one-based
<code>start</code> and <code>end</code> offsets. Optional output fields include
confidence, entity type, and normalized value.

```{r}
recognizer <- entity_recognizer(
  id = "project/member-id",
  entity_type = "MEMBER_ID",
  version = "1.0",
  recognize = function(text) {
    hit <- regexpr("\\bMEM-[0-9]{4}\\b", text, perl = TRUE)
    if (hit[[1]] < 0) {
      return(data.frame())
    }
    data.frame(
      start = as.integer(hit[[1]]),
      end = as.integer(hit[[1]] + attr(hit, "match.length") - 1L)
    )
  }
)
```

Validate every span before returning it. Recognizer errors are skipped with a
warning, so tests should cover invalid and boundary offsets.

## Adding a Guardrail Provider

<code>guardrail_provider()</code> is the narrow extension contract for a local
or remote detector. Its function receives <code>text</code>,
<code>stage</code>, and <code>metadata</code>, then returns findings.

```{r}
provider <- guardrail_provider(
  id = "project/detector",
  version = "1.0",
  stages = c("prompt", "output"),
  on_error = "block",
  scan = function(text, stage, metadata) {
    list()
  }
)
```

Provider work should define:

- whether content leaves the process;
- supported stages;
- version evidence;
- timeout and retry behavior;
- fail-closed or explicit fail-open behavior;
- normalized findings;
- tests with mocked responses and errors.

Keep external services and executables optional. They belong in
<code>Suggests</code> or behind runtime checks unless the core package cannot
function without them.

## Adding a Chat Provider Path

The main path is provider neutral. <code>secure_chat()</code> delegates
provider construction to <code>ellmer::chat()</code>. New provider-specific
wrappers should be avoided unless they add a distinct safety boundary. Use:

```{r}
secure_chat(
  prompt = "Approved prompt.",
  provider = "provider_name",
  model = "model-name",
  provider_args = list()
)
```

Credentials remain the provider SDK's responsibility. Never inspect, print, or
store provider keys in reports or audits.

## Tests

Tests are grouped by behavior:

| Test file | Main coverage |
|---|---|
| <code>test-policy.R</code> | Policy construction, rules, thresholds |
| <code>test-scan-prompt.R</code> | Prompt rules, normalization, redaction |
| <code>test-scan-context.R</code> | RAG anomalies, sources, authorization |
| <code>test-scan-output.R</code> | Output findings and actions |
| <code>test-secure-chat.R</code> | End-to-end orchestration |
| <code>test-reviewer-checks.R</code> | Semantic-review contracts and failures |
| <code>test-rate-guard.R</code> | Reservation, rollback, concurrency |
| <code>test-audit.R</code> | Privacy modes and persistence |
| <code>test-trust-boundary.R</code> | Model and host validation |
| <code>test-roadmap-upgrades.R</code> | Cross-feature upgrade regressions |
| <code>test-2026-stats.R</code> | OWASP 2026 metadata and statistics |

Use mocks for model and HTTP behavior. The normal test suite must not require
credentials, internet access, Ollama, Presidio, OPA, Gitleaks, or another
external process.

## Evaluation Data

<code>inst/extdata/security_eval_cases.csv</code> is a compact, transparent
starter corpus. Add a regression row when a behavior gap should remain visible
across policies. Keep private or large application corpora outside the package.

The opt-in benchmark at
<code>inst/scripts/benchmark-security-eval.R</code> is for adoption and release
checks that do not belong in routine unit tests.

## Documentation Workflow

Public functions need roxygen documentation, useful examples, and a place in
the pkgdown reference index. User-facing behavior changes also need README,
vignette, and NEWS updates where relevant.

Typical commands are:

```{r}
devtools::document()
devtools::test()
devtools::check()
pkgdown::build_site()
```

Do not put live API requests in evaluated examples. Provider examples should
use <code>eval = FALSE</code>, read credentials from environment variables,
and use placeholders rather than real secrets.

## Compatibility and Deprecation

Use R's standard deprecation mechanism when replacing a public path. Keep the
compatibility wrapper long enough for users to migrate, name the replacement in
the message, document the change, and add a regression test.

<code>shield_gemini()</code> and <code>shield_ollama()</code> demonstrate this
pattern by forwarding users to <code>secure_chat(provider = ...)</code>.

## Review Checklist

Before merging a change:

1. Confirm the public contract and default behavior.
2. Check failure behavior at every external boundary.
3. Add positive, negative, and privacy regression tests.
4. Confirm metadata-only audits remove new content fields.
5. Confirm statistics do not expose prompts or credentials.
6. Keep remote calls and optional binaries out of package checks.
7. Review CRAN dependencies and conditional imports.
8. Update generated documentation.
9. Run package checks in a clean session.
10. Record user-visible changes in <code>NEWS.md</code>.
